insurer: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified (Base Sum Insured + Booster+ Sum Insured + Safeguard/Safeguard+ Sum Insured as per Policy Schedule)

great.name: Room rent (No limit / Any room) — default hospitalization cover
great.quote: “We don’t limit your choice. Choose the room you like, but choose judiciously to protect your Sum Insured.”
great.explanation: This indicates no default room-rent capping (you can choose any room). This is best-in-class; higher room categories can still increase overall bills and consume your Sum Insured faster.

great.name: Built-in additional Sum Insured buffer / unlimited reinstatement-style cover (ReAssure ‘Forever’)
great.quote: “Enjoy unlimited Sum Insured. The first paid claim in the life of the policy triggers ReAssure ‘Forever’. Once Triggered it stays for life, provided that the policy is renewed without break.”
great.explanation: After the first paid claim, the policy provides an extra buffer that can repeatedly support future claims (subject to per-claim cap up to Base Sum Insured). This materially increases claim-paying ability beyond base SI.

great.name: Consumables / non-payable items covered (via Safeguard / Safeguard+)
great.quote: “Claim Safeguard: We will cover non-payable items mentioned in ‘List I – Expenses not covered’ of Annexure I’.”
great.explanation: Consumables and other ‘non-payable’ items (e.g., gloves, masks etc.) are typically out-of-pocket; here they are covered when Safeguard/Safeguard+ is chosen, reducing surprise hospital bill deductions.

good.name: Pre-existing disease (PED) waiting period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy.”
good.explanation: 36 months PED waiting is within the standard/acceptable range (not a red flag). PED coverage starts after completion of this continuous period (subject to declaration and acceptance).

good.name: Specific illness waiting period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of the listed conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy.”
good.explanation: 24 months is standard for listed specific illnesses/procedures.

good.name: Initial waiting period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of any Illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident…”
good.explanation: 30 days initial waiting is standard for illnesses (accidents are covered from day 1).

good.name: Pre-hospitalization cover
good.quote: “We will pay expenses incurred on consultations, medicines, physiotherapy, diagnostic tests for 60 days before the date of admission…”
good.explanation: 60 days pre-hospitalization is market-standard to good.

good.name: Post-hospitalization cover
good.quote: “…and 180 days after date of discharge IF these are related to the condition for which hospitalization claim is paid.”
good.explanation: 180 days post-hospitalization is solid industry standard.

good.name: Domiciliary / Home Care treatment covered
good.quote: “Home Care Treatment means treatment availed by the insured person at home which in normal course would require care and treatment at a hospital but is actually taken at home…”
good.explanation: Domiciliary/home care coverage is a meaningful add-on benefit for cases where treatment is medically advised at home (subject to conditions).

bad.name: No restore benefit (Sum Insured is NOT replenished after a claim)
bad.quote: No restore/reinstatement clause found in the provided policy wording extract. The policy instead describes ReAssure+/ReAssureX and Booster+ mechanisms.
bad.reference: Mandatory feature check (Restore Benefit) — not explicitly stated
bad.explanation: A standard ‘restore/reinstatement of base SI within the policy year’ benefit is not explicitly stated here. If you want a classic restore feature, confirm from the insurer/policy schedule; otherwise assume it is not available.

bad.name: NCB / Renewal bonus not found (Sum Insured does not grow at renewal by NCB)
bad.quote: No explicit “No Claim Bonus / Cumulative Bonus increase at renewal” benefit statement found (other than wellness discount and inflation-linked Safeguard/Safeguard+).
bad.reference: Mandatory feature check (NCB/Renewal Bonus) — not explicitly stated
bad.explanation: If there is no explicit NCB/renewal bonus, your Sum Insured may not increase just because you had no claims. (Note: Booster+ and Safeguard/Safeguard+ are different mechanisms and are not stated as NCB.)

bad.name: Air ambulance has a sub-limit
bad.quote: “Air Ambulance: Only in case of Emergency. Maximum INR 2,50,000 per hospitalization.”
bad.explanation: Air ambulance is covered but capped at ₹2.5 lakh per hospitalization; costs can exceed this in many cities.

bad.name: Modern treatments list appears restricted to specified items
bad.quote: “We pay for Modern treatments as specified below:”
bad.explanation: Coverage is tied to a defined list of modern treatments in the wording. If a required modern procedure is not within this list, it may not be covered as a ‘modern treatment’ benefit.

bad.name: Proportionate deduction if you choose a room higher than your eligible category (can reduce claim payouts in room-modified plans)
bad.quote: “If you opt for a Hospital room which is higher than the eligible room category as specified in your Policy Schedule, then We will pay only a pro-rated portion of the total Associated Medical Expenses…”
bad.explanation: If your policy schedule has an eligible room category (e.g., sharing/single) and you take a higher category, the insurer may apply pro-rata on associated medical expenses—this can materially reduce claim payout. This is especially relevant because the policy allows Room Type Modification.

unclear.name: Co-pay (percentage and when it applies) not specified in wording excerpt
unclear.quote: “Co-Payment: It is the percentage of admissible claim amount You would have to bear, Rest we will pay.”
unclear.explanation: The clause defines co-pay but does not state the actual % or when it applies by default. This is typically shown in the Policy Schedule/plan option—verify your selected co-pay and whether it is optional or mandatory.

unclear.name: Room Type Modification — default eligible room category depends on plan/schedule
unclear.quote: “You can as per your lifestyle, choose to change the room category we are offering… You can choose between a Single Private Room and a Sharing Room.”
unclear.explanation: The policy indicates you can choose single private or sharing room, but the default eligibility (and whether ‘any room’ applies across all variants) is tied to what you select / what is in your Policy Schedule. Confirm your schedule to avoid pro-rata deductions.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
